version: Gabrys et al. (2018) final 18-item English, Table 1 administration ordering
rights_evidence: Publisher Copyright section explicitly permits distribution or reproduction in other forums under CC BY; license link resolves to 4.0. Newly developed 116-item pool reduced to final 18. Table 1 has no third-party exclusion, only reverse/factor/order notes.
language: English source; no verified Chinese version acquired; any project Chinese translation must be labelled unvalidated working translation.
instructions_en: The purpose of this questionnaire is to determine what you generally think/feel/do when stressful situations provoke negative thoughts and emotions. Of course, you may act differently depending on the situation, but try to think of what you usually think/feel/do when you are stressed or upset. Using the scale below, indicate the extent to which agree or disagree with the following statements.
timeframe: General/usually; no fixed recent recall period.

items.text_en: I weigh out my options before choosing how to take action.
I feel like I lose control over my thoughts and emotions.
I approach the situation from multiple angles.
It’s difficult to let go of intrusive thoughts or emotions.
I consider the situation for multiple viewpoints before responding.
I take the time to think of several ways to best cope with the situation before acting.
I find it easy to set-aside unpleasant thoughts or emotions.
It is easy for me to ignore distracting thoughts.
I can easily think of multiple coping options before deciding how to respond.
I take the time to see things from different perspectives before reacting.
I get easily distracted by upsetting thoughts or feelings.
I take the time to think of more than one way to resolve the problem.
I control my thoughts and feelings by putting the situation into context.
I can remain in control of my thoughts and emotions.
I have a hard time managing my emotions.
My thoughts and emotions interfere with my ability to concentrate.
I manage my thoughts or feelings by reframing the situation.
It’s hard for me to shift my attention away from negative thoughts or feelings.

scoring.total: Do not create a global total: source operationalizes two means.
scoring.missing_response: No source rule established; use complete response requirement as platform policy.

evidence.development_study: Study 1 students N300 and community adults N302; Study 2 N368 students; Study 3 N47 females.
evidence.limits: Self-perceived cognitive skills, not performance test or diagnosis; sample results are not clinical cutoffs. ±1 SD high/low labels in regression plots are analytic contrasts, not patient bands.

implementation_notes: Freeze Table 1 wording and final administration order in its rightmost parentheses; do not treat leftmost table row number as item order.
Do not import initial 44-item supplement or silently mix Table 5 variant ordering/wording.
No source-verified full Chinese administration page; working translation can be openly redistributed with attribution under CC BY4.
Report two self-reflection scores, no diagnosis or forced emotional-suppression advice.
report_suggestion_zh: 报告为“压力情境中注意力与情绪的调节感”“考虑不同解释与应对办法的灵活感”。可以建议暂停片刻，列出两种可能解释与两种行动选择；不建议强行压制正常情绪，也不称为ACT心理灵活性总分。
